back: Pay for each hour worked; overtime is paid at a premium for hours beyond the normal week.
Pay for each unit produced, so earnings rise with output; quality may suffer.
A percentage of the value of sales, often added to a basic wage; suits sales staff.
A share of the firm's profit divided among employees, linking pay to the success of the business.
Extra pay linked to how well an employee, team or business meets agreed targets, judged by appraisal.
Non-cash benefits, such as a company vehicle, medical aid or a housing allowance, in addition to pay.
Pay = normal hours × rate + overtime hours × (rate × overtime multiple).
Herzberg: pay is a hygiene factor; it prevents dissatisfaction but does not alone create lasting motivation.
Ask: can output be measured? does quality or teamwork matter more? can the business afford it? Variable pay costs more only when output or sales rise.
